text.en:
When the trees on the hill were cut, the stream near Mani's village dried up and the monsoon floods washed away the soil.
His teacher said, "Forests are like sponges. They hold water and soil."
The village decided to plant new trees.

Forests are large areas full of trees, plants and animals. They give us wood, fruits, medicines, honey and many other things.
Trees give out oxygen, take in carbon dioxide, hold the soil with their roots, bring rain and give shade. Forests are homes to many animals and birds.
We protect forests by not cutting trees without need, planting new trees, preventing forest fires and protecting wild animals. Many communities, such as the Bishnois of Rajasthan, have protected trees for centuries.
Forests give us wood, fruit, honey and medicines.
Trees give oxygen, hold the soil and bring rain.
Forests are homes of many animals and birds.
We protect forests by planting trees and not cutting them without need.

problem.en: What can happen if too many trees on a hill are cut?

text.en: Roots no longer hold the soil.
Heavy rain washes the soil away and causes floods.
Animals also lose their homes. So we must protect forests.

prompt.en: A friend says cutting one tree does not matter. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: If everyone cuts a tree, a forest disappears.
We should plant a tree for every one we cut.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking small actions never add up.

points.en: Forests give us many useful things.
Trees give oxygen and hold soil.
